newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's press says Israel pushing region to war.
newsitem.headline: Syria's press says Israel pushing region to war.

text.p: Syria's official newspapers accused Israel on Saturday of pushing the region to war by taking the first step towards building 900 new housing units for Jews on the occupied Golan Heights.

State-run newspapers said the move showed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did not want to make peace with Syria and called for world pressure on Israel to stop its settlement activities.

"Israel's moves to build more settlemnts and to bring thousands of Israelis to the Golan, shows that Israel, under Netanyahu and the extremist rabbis and generals, is deliberately trying to escalate tension in the region," Tishreen daily said.
"Netanyahu's government does not only want to undermine the peace process but also to detonate the situation in the region and return it once again to the cycle of wars and disasters."
Syria and Israel conducted war games in recent weeks in and near the Golan amid exchanged accusations that the other side was preparing for war. The two said they were not planning any attacks.
Israeli officials said on Friday the government had taken the first step towards building 900 new housing units on the Golan, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
The units are part of a Golan Jewish settler plan to add a total of 2,500 homes for Israelis on the heights by the year 2000, they said.

Syria, which has held five years of sporadic peace talks with Israel, had strongly condemned Netanyahu who refuses to trade the occupied Arab lands for peace and has authorised the expansion of settlements in the West Bank and Gaza.
No talks have been held since Netanyahu took office in June and Damascus says it will not resume negotiations until Israel agrees to withdraw fully from the Golan.
Al-Thawra daily said the settlement moves were hindering efforts by the United States and other international parties to revive the peace process.
"The dangerous Jewish settlement programme is a message from Netanyahu's government to Arabs and the world that israel rejects peace and the peace efforts," al-Thawra said.

"The settlements constitute a direct aggression against Arabs at a time while the world is exerting efforts to resume the peace process which is threatened with death due to Netanyahu's policies," the paper said.
"Netanyahu's government is publically and practically escalating the conflict and killing the U.S. peace initiative," it said.

Al-Thawra called for an "effective international pressure to force the Israeli government stop settlements and commit itself to the basis of the peace process especially the land-for-peace principle in order to provide the climate which will allow the resumption of this process".
